title: DELETE /sites/{id} silently no-ops when the id does not exist
description:
Found while fixing auritus-b0f217. \`_delete_site\` in
\`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py\` does:

\`\`\`python
def _delete_site(site_id: str, headers: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    _require_operator(headers)
    _sites.delete_item(Key={"site_id": site_id})
    return _response(200, {"site_id": site_id, "deleted": True})
\`\`\`

DynamoDB's \`delete_item\` succeeds silently whether or not the key exists.
Calling \`DELETE /sites/anything-at-all\` returns \`200 {"deleted": true}\`
regardless of whether a site with that id ever existed. This is how the
original site-key-lifecycle bug report's claim ("passing site_key to revoke
works") went unnoticed for so long: it wasn't actually revoking anything,
just returning a false-positive success.

## Fix

Load the item first; raise \`LookupError("site_not_found")\` when absent
(matches the pattern already used by \`_delete_admin_job\` in the M10 epic).
Small, low-priority, not user-facing in a way anyone has hit yet.
